course_name_en: Introduction to Automatic Control: Temporal Aspects
prerequisites: Linear differential equations with constant coefficients: recognize them; solve them; know properties of the derivation and the integration operators.
Perform operations in the algebra of polynomials.
Have a very basic knowledge of programming and algorithms.

learning_outcomes.text: Be able to identify a system and its associated physical quantities.
Have knowledge of modeling a dynamic system based on physical knowledge using the Laplace transform and simple models (1st and 2nd order).
Autonomous on the usage of block diagrams as a representation of system functioning.
Be able to quantify characteristics of a temporal response of a system (stability, precision, speed, robustness).
Be familiar with the advantages and limitations of simple control laws (open/closed loop and basic correctors).
Know how to perform basic calculations and usage of the MATLAB/Simulink software.
Be able to implement simple control laws to save energy and meet specific requirements.

syllabus_topics: Presentation of the lecturer
Introduction to automatic control and its tools
Definition of what automatic control is.
Where is it found - examples in the fields taught at ENIT.
The interest of automatic control in societal issues (ecology, accessibility and limiting inequalities).
Definition of what a system is and the assumptions of the course.
Introduction to the benefits of modelling a system.
Presentation of the Laplace transformation (hypothesis, advantages).
Definition of a transfer function.
Systems analysis - Systems of 1st order
Reminder of the assumptions made in the course about the systems and models studied.
Reminder of the Laplace transform and transfer functions.
Introduction to the different possible inputs for a system.
Introduction to the block diagram tool.
First-order model - The different types of response.
Initial and final value theorem
Identification of a first order system.
Systems analysis - Systems of 2nd order
Reminder of the Laplace transform, block diagrams and Theorems.
Reminder of the different types of inputs.
Reminder of systems modelled by a 1st order.
The different response types of systems modelled by a 2nd order.
Identifying the parameters of a second-order response.
Positioning the poles to predict stability.
Controlled system - Stability - Performance.
The concept of control - Open and Closed Loop.
Diagram of a controlled system.
Transfer function of a controlled system and classical responses.
Concept of stability.
Routh's criterion.
System performance.
Basic correctors (digital, proportional, etc.)
Opening up to corrective measures aimed at reducing consumption.
teaching_methods: Classroom lectures with interactive parts (the correction of exercises).
Slides and different handouts with theoretical and applied exercises (with all levels of difficulty).
Practical work on physical setups with an oral assessment.
Autonomous work using the Moodle platform as well as the MATLAB software platform.
assessment_rules: The evaluation formula is (1*DS1 + 1*CC1)/2. Assessment is done by a graded grid.
